title: About
text:
I’m a data scientist and amateur musician. Here is where I write up the math and statistics I’m learning as an educational piece — proofs, derivations, the occasional simulation in Python or R — mostly as a way of forcing myself to actually understand something rather than just recognize it. Right now that means working through Bayesian learning and inference, alongside classical piano and electric guitar on the side.
I also enjoy learning music theory, philosophy, political theory, and theology. Not an expert by any means — I’m mostly interested in how an argument develops and how structure glues together.
This is mostly a journal, not a polished blog. Expect worked-through problems, half-finished intuitions, and the occasional political or philosophical tangent — posted as I go, not on a schedule.

title: A simulation example
text:
Claim
Let \(X_1, \dots, X_n \overset{iid}{\sim} \text{Uniform}(0,1)\). By the CLT,
\[
\sqrt{n}\left(\bar{X}_n - \tfrac{1}{2}\right) \xrightarrow{d} \mathcal{N}\!\left(0, \tfrac{1}{12}\right).
\]

title: A simulation example
text:
Check it with a simulation


Code
# Set eval: true (and have matplotlib/numpy installed) to actually run this
# at render time. Left as eval: false here so the starter repo builds
# instantly with no dependencies.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

n, trials = 30, 10000
means = np.mean(np.random.uniform(0, 1, size=(trials, n)), axis=1)
scaled = np.sqrt(n) * (means - 0.5)

plt.hist(scaled, bins=50, density=True)
plt.title("Simulated distribution vs. CLT prediction")
plt.show()
